title: 'The biggest shift happens when AI stops being a tool people occasionally use and becomes part of the operational…
excerpt: We speak to Arm's EVP of Cloud AI on what is really changing at the infrastructure layer
content_html:
As AI systems continue to evolve and advance, it's not just data center architecture being affected, but the wider infrastructure industry as a whole.

As Agentic AI workloads continue to scale, it is the CPU layer being particularly affected, with efficiency, coordination, and cost per task become increasingly important defining factors.

We spoke to Mohamed Awad, EVP, Cloud AI at Arm, to find out more.

  • Gartner predicts that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by 2027 due to operationalization difficulties. How does Arm’s approach to "system-level" architecture specifically address the friction points, like cost and complexity, that are causing these cancellations?

I think the Gartner prediction reinforces something we’re hearing broadly across the industry. Most organizations aren’t struggling because today’s models aren’t capable enough. They’re struggling because operationalizing AI at scale is fundamentally different from demonstrating it in a pilot.

At the largest scale, we're seeing many of the same operational challenges play out in the physical world as well. Building AI infrastructure now means solving for power, supply chains, land, permitting, and deployment timelines just as much as advances in compute.

Moving from a handful of AI interactions to continuous, production-grade workflows requires a much more holistic view of the infrastructure stack – but it also requires organizations to rethink how AI interacts with their existing data and business processes. AI performs best where information is structured and workflows are well understood. As organizations extend AI into more complex enterprise environments, both the infrastructure and the operational environment have to evolve together.

That’s why we’ve focused on optimizing the system, from the CPU and platform through to the software ecosystem. As organizations move from pilots to production, success will increasingly depend on how efficiently their entire infrastructure works together – not just how capable any individual model or processor is.

  • We’ve seen companies like Uber exhaust their AI budgets in months due to unstructured prompting costs. How does moving intelligence from ad-hoc tools to a "central intelligence layer" anchored by Arm CPUs change the economic ROI for an enterprise?

I'd actually look at examples like Uber a little differently. Rather than signaling that AI is too expensive, they demonstrate how much value organizations are finding when AI is deployed successfully. The challenge is that demand is growing faster than the infrastructure needed to support it economically.

That's why we're seeing AI token economics improve at an extraordinary pace as models, silicon, software, and inference infrastructure become more efficient. At the same time, organizations are learning to redesign workflows rather than simply replacing existing processes with AI. Together, those trends are helping make AI more economical to deploy at scale.

Arm's role is helping drive that efficiency by optimizing AI infrastructure from the ground up. Improving performance, memory bandwidth utilization, and energy efficiency across the compute platform helps lower both capital and operating costs as organizations scale AI.

  • You’ve argued that AI’s true economic impact will come from turning AI into reliable operational capacity. How does Arm help businesses transition from "casual experimentation" to high-throughput, daily business operations?

The biggest shift happens when AI stops being a tool people occasionally use and becomes part of the operational fabric of the business. At that point, reliability, latency, security, and efficiency become just as important as model capability.

Our role is to provide the compute foundation that helps make that transition possible at scale. We’re part of the broader industry effort to optimize AI infrastructure across silicon, platforms, and software so organizations can deploy AI more efficiently and economically in everyday operations. Ultimately, the goal isn’t simply to automate work – it’s to make AI reliable enough to help people accomplish more as part of their everyday workflows.

  • While GPUs dominated the first wave of AI, the "agentic era" seems to be hitting a bottleneck at the coordination layer. Why is the CPU now the defining factor in whether an agentic workflow - which might check a CRM, update a database, and trigger a task - actually succeeds?

GPUs remain fundamental for training models and accelerating inference. What’s changing is everything that happens around those models.

Every time an agent retrieves enterprise data, coordinates multiple models, invokes external tools, or manages a business workflow, those activities depend heavily on the CPU. As organizations deploy more autonomous AI systems, those system-level workloads continue to grow, making the CPU an increasingly important part of delivering efficient AI infrastructure.

The question is no longer simply “How fast can I execute a model?” It’s “How efficiently can I execute an entire AI workflow?”

  • The new Arm AGI CPU claims more than 2x performance per rack compared with x86 platforms. What specific architectural choices were made in this "historic first" production silicon to handle the continuous, system-level workloads of agentic AI?

Agentic AI places fundamentally different demands on infrastructure than traditional cloud computing. Rather than optimizing for peak benchmark performance, we designed Arm AGI CPU around the realities of modern AI data centers – fixed power, cooling, rack density, and continuous system-level workloads. That means optimizing how data moves through the system – from compute and memory bandwidth to efficient bandwidth utilization – so the CPU can orchestrate the continuous data movement, coordination, and reasoning workloads that agentic AI creates.

The objective wasn’t simply to build a faster CPU. It was to help organizations deploy more useful AI within the physical and economic constraints that increasingly define AI infrastructure.

  • With Oracle Cloud joining the Arm AGI ecosystem and Google Cloud deploying Axion, we are seeing a massive shift toward custom Arm silicon. Does this signal the end of "general-purpose" data center architecture in favor of purpose-built agentic infrastructure?

I don’t think the story is custom silicon versus commercial platforms. What’s changing is that organizations increasingly want infrastructure optimized for the AI workloads they’re running, while maintaining the flexibility of a broad software ecosystem.

We’re seeing that play out in different ways across the Arm ecosystem. Many hyperscalers are building their own silicon while also deploying commercially available Arm-based platforms, including Arm AGI CPU. Both approaches reflect the same underlying trend: AI infrastructure is becoming more purpose-built, but customers still want the portability and ecosystem scale that comes from a common architecture.

  • Many agentic AI projects risk overtaking data center capacity. How does Arm’s emphasis on performance-per-watt allow organizations to scale agentic AI within existing air-cooled data centers without requiring massive new infrastructure builds?

Power has become one of the defining economic constraints of AI infrastructure. Organizations can’t assume they’ll always have another data center or another gigawatt available.

That changes how infrastructure is designed. Success increasingly depends on delivering more AI capability within existing power, cooling, and rack constraints. Performance per watt is no longer just an engineering metric – it’s becoming a business metric because it determines how much AI organizations can deploy without proportionally increasing infrastructure investment.

  • Industry reports suggest that AI will fundamentally alter role requirements, rewarding those who can transition from "operators" to "orchestrators". How is Arm’s hardware evolution supporting this shift in how work is actually redesigned?

As AI becomes embedded into everyday business operations, organizations increasingly need infrastructure that supports continuous coordination rather than isolated model execution.

Whether people are orchestrating AI agents or AI agents are orchestrating one another, the underlying infrastructure has to manage constant communication, context, and execution efficiently. That’s exactly the type of system-level workload we’re designing for. Ultimately, the goal isn’t to replace people – it’s to make AI reliable enough that people can spend less time coordinating work and more time creating value.

  • What is the risk to businesses and professionals who continue to rely on legacy industry paradigms while a new cohort of "AI-native" teams builds on top of agentic-ready infrastructure?

Organizations that continue treating AI as a standalone productivity tool may find it harder to capture the full operational benefits of agentic AI. The next phase isn’t simply about adopting more models – it’s about building infrastructure capable of supporting continuous AI operations across the business.

Organizations that begin building this capability early won’t just deploy AI sooner – they’ll learn faster. As teams begin redesigning workflows around AI, they build the experience needed to improve those systems over time. We’re already seeing that in areas like software development, where AI-native teams are moving well beyond simple code generation toward entirely new ways of building software.

sentences.zh: 为什么 CPU 现在是代理工作流程（可能检查 CRM、更新数据库并触发任务）是否真正成功的决定性因素？

blocks.html_en: GPUs remain fundamental for training models and accelerating inference. What’s changing is everything that happens around those models.

sentences.en: GPUs remain fundamental for training models and accelerating inference.
sentences.zh: GPU 仍然是训练模型和加速推理的基础。

sentences.en: What’s changing is everything that happens around those models.
sentences.zh: 正在改变的是围绕这些模型发生的一切。

blocks.html_en: Every time an agent retrieves enterprise data, coordinates multiple models, invokes external tools, or manages a business workflow, those activities depend heavily on the CPU. As organizations deploy more autonomous AI systems, those system-level workloads continue to grow, making the CPU an increasingly important part of delivering efficient AI infrastructure.

sentences.en: Every time an agent retrieves enterprise data, coordinates multiple models, invokes external tools, or manages a business workflow, those activities depend heavily on the CPU.
sentences.zh: 每次代理检索企业数据、协调多个模型、调用外部工具或管理业务工作流程时，这些活动都严重依赖于 CPU。

sentences.en: As organizations deploy more autonomous AI systems, those system-level workloads continue to grow, making the CPU an increasingly important part of delivering efficient AI infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 随着组织部署更多自主人工智能系统，这些系统级工作负载不断增长，使得 CPU 成为提供高效人工智能基础设施的日益重要的组成部分。

blocks.html_en: The question is no longer simply “How fast can I execute a model?” It’s “How efficiently can I execute an entire AI workflow?”

sentences.en: The question is no longer simply “How fast can I execute a model?”
sentences.zh: 问题不再是简单的“我能以多快的速度执行模型？”

sentences.en: It’s “How efficiently can I execute an entire AI workflow?”
sentences.zh: 问题是“我能多有效地执行整个人工智能工作流程？”

blocks.html_en: • The new Arm AGI CPU claims more than 2x performance per rack compared with x86 platforms. What specific architectural choices were made in this "historic first" production silicon to handle the continuous, system-level workloads of agentic AI?

sentences.en: The new Arm AGI CPU claims more than 2x performance per rack compared with x86 platforms.
sentences.zh: 与 x86 平台相比，新的 Arm AGI CPU 声称每个机架的性能提高了 2 倍以上。

sentences.en: What specific architectural choices were made in this "historic first" production silicon to handle the continuous, system-level workloads of agentic AI?
sentences.zh: 在这个“历史性的首次”生产芯片中做出了哪些具体的架构选择来处理代理人工智能的连续、系统级工作负载？

blocks.html_en: Agentic AI places fundamentally different demands on infrastructure than traditional cloud computing. Rather than optimizing for peak benchmark performance, we designed Arm AGI CPU around the realities of modern AI data centers – fixed power, cooling, rack density, and continuous system-level workloads. That means optimizing how data moves through the system – from compute and memory bandwidth to efficient bandwidth utilization – so the CPU can orchestrate the continuous data movement, coordination, and reasoning workloads that agentic AI creates.

sentences.en: Agentic AI places fundamentally different demands on infrastructure than traditional cloud computing.
sentences.zh: 代理人工智能对基础设施提出了与传统云计算根本不同的要求。

sentences.en: Rather than optimizing for peak benchmark performance, we designed Arm AGI CPU around the realities of modern AI data centers – fixed power, cooling, rack density, and continuous system-level workloads.
sentences.zh: 我们没有针对峰值基准性能进行优化，而是围绕现代 AI 数据中心的实际情况（固定功耗、冷却、机架密度和连续系统级工作负载）设计了 Arm AGI CPU。

sentences.en: That means optimizing how data moves through the system – from compute and memory bandwidth to efficient bandwidth utilization – so the CPU can orchestrate the continuous data movement, coordination, and reasoning workloads that agentic AI creates.
sentences.zh: 这意味着优化数据在系统中的移动方式（从计算和内存带宽到高效的带宽利用），以便 CPU 可以协调代理 AI 创建的连续数据移动、协调和推理工作负载。

blocks.html_en: The objective wasn’t simply to build a faster CPU. It was to help organizations deploy more useful AI within the physical and economic constraints that increasingly define AI infrastructure.

sentences.en: The objective wasn’t simply to build a faster CPU.
sentences.zh: 目标不仅仅是构建更快的 CPU。

sentences.en: It was to help organizations deploy more useful AI within the physical and economic constraints that increasingly define AI infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 它是为了帮助组织在日益定义人工智能基础设施的物理和经济限制内部署更有用的人工智能。

blocks.html_en: • With Oracle Cloud joining the Arm AGI ecosystem and Google Cloud deploying Axion, we are seeing a massive shift toward custom Arm silicon. Does this signal the end of "general-purpose" data center architecture in favor of purpose-built agentic infrastructure?

sentences.en: With Oracle Cloud joining the Arm AGI ecosystem and Google Cloud deploying Axion, we are seeing a massive shift toward custom Arm silicon.
sentences.zh: 随着 Oracle Cloud 加入 Arm AGI 生态系统以及 Google Cloud 部署 Axion，我们看到了向定制 Arm 芯片的巨大转变。

sentences.en: Does this signal the end of "general-purpose" data center architecture in favor of purpose-built agentic infrastructure?
sentences.zh: 这是否标志着“通用”数据中心架构的终结，转而采用专门构建的代理基础设施？

blocks.html_en: I don’t think the story is custom silicon versus commercial platforms. What’s changing is that organizations increasingly want infrastructure optimized for the AI workloads they’re running, while maintaining the flexibility of a broad software ecosystem.

sentences.en: I don’t think the story is custom silicon versus commercial platforms.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这个故事是定制芯片与商业平台的对比。

sentences.en: What’s changing is that organizations increasingly want infrastructure optimized for the AI workloads they’re running, while maintaining the flexibility of a broad software ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 正在发生的变化是，组织越来越希望基础设施能够针对其运行的人工智能工作负载进行优化，同时保持广泛软件生态系统的灵活性。

blocks.html_en: We’re seeing that play out in different ways across the Arm ecosystem. Many hyperscalers are building their own silicon while also deploying commercially available Arm-based platforms, including Arm AGI CPU. Both approaches reflect the same underlying trend: AI infrastructure is becoming more purpose-built, but customers still want the portability and ecosystem scale that comes from a common architecture.

sentences.en: We’re seeing that play out in different ways across the Arm ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 我们看到这种情况在 Arm 生态系统中以不同的方式发挥作用。

sentences.en: Many hyperscalers are building their own silicon while also deploying commercially available Arm-based platforms, including Arm AGI CPU.
sentences.zh: 许多超大规模企业正在构建自己的芯片，同时还部署基于 Arm 的商用平台，包括 Arm AGI CPU。

sentences.en: Both approaches reflect the same underlying trend: AI infrastructure is becoming more purpose-built, but customers still want the portability and ecosystem scale that comes from a common architecture.
sentences.zh: 这两种方法都反映了相同的基本趋势：人工智能基础设施变得更加专用，但客户仍然希望来自通用架构的可移植性和生态系统规模。

blocks.html_en: • Many agentic AI projects risk overtaking data center capacity. How does Arm’s emphasis on performance-per-watt allow organizations to scale agentic AI within existing air-cooled data centers without requiring massive new infrastructure builds?

sentences.en: Many agentic AI projects risk overtaking data center capacity.
sentences.zh: 许多代理人工智能项目都面临着超过数据中心容量的风险。

sentences.en: How does Arm’s emphasis on performance-per-watt allow organizations to scale agentic AI within existing air-cooled data centers without requiring massive new infrastructure builds?
sentences.zh: Arm 对每瓦性能的重视如何让组织能够在现有风冷数据中心内扩展代理 AI，而不需要大规模的新基础设施建设？

blocks.html_en: Power has become one of the defining economic constraints of AI infrastructure. Organizations can’t assume they’ll always have another data center or another gigawatt available.

sentences.en: Power has become one of the defining economic constraints of AI infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 电力已成为人工智能基础设施的决定性经济约束之一。

sentences.en: Organizations can’t assume they’ll always have another data center or another gigawatt available.
sentences.zh: 组织不能假设他们总是有另一个数据中心或另一个可用的千兆瓦电力。

blocks.html_en: That changes how infrastructure is designed. Success increasingly depends on delivering more AI capability within existing power, cooling, and rack constraints. Performance per watt is no longer just an engineering metric – it’s becoming a business metric because it determines how much AI organizations can deploy without proportionally increasing infrastructure investment.

sentences.en: That changes how infrastructure is designed.
sentences.zh: 这改变了基础设施的设计方式。

sentences.en: Success increasingly depends on delivering more AI capability within existing power, cooling, and rack constraints.
sentences.zh: 成功越来越依赖于在现有电源、冷却和机架限制下提供更多人工智能功能。

sentences.en: Performance per watt is no longer just an engineering metric – it’s becoming a business metric because it determines how much AI organizations can deploy without proportionally increasing infrastructure investment.
sentences.zh: 每瓦性能不再只是一个工程指标，它正在成为一个业务指标，因为它决定了组织在不按比例增加基础设施投资的情况下可以部署多少人工智能。

blocks.html_en: • Industry reports suggest that AI will fundamentally alter role requirements, rewarding those who can transition from "operators" to "orchestrators". How is Arm’s hardware evolution supporting this shift in how work is actually redesigned?

sentences.en: Industry reports suggest that AI will fundamentally alter role requirements, rewarding those who can transition from "operators" to "orchestrators".
sentences.zh: 行业报告表明，人工智能将从根本上改变角色要求，奖励那些能够从“操作员”转变为“编排者”的人。

sentences.en: How is Arm’s hardware evolution supporting this shift in how work is actually redesigned?
sentences.zh: Arm 的硬件演变如何支持工作实际重新设计方式的转变？

blocks.html_en: As AI becomes embedded into everyday business operations, organizations increasingly need infrastructure that supports continuous coordination rather than isolated model execution.

sentences.en: As AI becomes embedded into everyday business operations, organizations increasingly need infrastructure that supports continuous coordination rather than isolated model execution.
sentences.zh: 随着人工智能嵌入到日常业务运营中，组织越来越需要支持持续协调而不是孤立的模型执行的基础设施。

blocks.html_en: Whether people are orchestrating AI agents or AI agents are orchestrating one another, the underlying infrastructure has to manage constant communication, context, and execution efficiently. That’s exactly the type of system-level workload we’re designing for. Ultimately, the goal isn’t to replace people – it’s to make AI reliable enough that people can spend less time coordinating work and more time creating value.

sentences.en: Whether people are orchestrating AI agents or AI agents are orchestrating one another, the underlying infrastructure has to manage constant communication, context, and execution efficiently.
sentences.zh: 无论是人们在编排人工智能代理，还是人工智能代理相互协调，底层基础设施都必须有效地管理持续的通信、上下文和执行。

sentences.en: That’s exactly the type of system-level workload we’re designing for.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们设计的系统级工作负载类型。

sentences.en: Ultimately, the goal isn’t to replace people – it’s to make AI reliable enough that people can spend less time coordinating work and more time creating value.
sentences.zh: 最终，我们的目标不是取代人类，而是让人工智能足够可靠，让人们可以花更少的时间协调工作，花更多的时间创造价值。

blocks.html_en: • What is the risk to businesses and professionals who continue to rely on legacy industry paradigms while a new cohort of "AI-native" teams builds on top of agentic-ready infrastructure?

sentences.en: What is the risk to businesses and professionals who continue to rely on legacy industry paradigms while a new cohort of "AI-native" teams builds on top of agentic-ready infrastructure?
sentences.zh: 当一批新的“人工智能原生”团队建立在代理就绪基础设施之上时，继续依赖传统行业范式的企业和专业人士面临哪些风险？

blocks.html_en: Organizations that continue treating AI as a standalone productivity tool may find it harder to capture the full operational benefits of agentic AI. The next phase isn’t simply about adopting more models – it’s about building infrastructure capable of supporting continuous AI operations across the business.

sentences.en: Organizations that continue treating AI as a standalone productivity tool may find it harder to capture the full operational benefits of agentic AI.
sentences.zh: 继续将人工智能视为独立生产力工具的组织可能会发现更难获得代理人工智能的全部运营优势。

sentences.en: The next phase isn’t simply about adopting more models – it’s about building infrastructure capable of supporting continuous AI operations across the business.
sentences.zh: 下一阶段不仅仅是采用更多模型，而是构建能够支持整个企业持续人工智能运营的基础设施。

blocks.html_en: Organizations that begin building this capability early won’t just deploy AI sooner – they’ll learn faster. As teams begin redesigning workflows around AI, they build the experience needed to improve those systems over time. We’re already seeing that in areas like software development, where AI-native teams are moving well beyond simple code generation toward entirely new ways of building software.

sentences.en: Organizations that begin building this capability early won’t just deploy AI sooner – they’ll learn faster.
sentences.zh: 尽早开始构建这种能力的组织不仅会更快地部署人工智能，而且会学得更快。

sentences.en: As teams begin redesigning workflows around AI, they build the experience needed to improve those systems over time.
sentences.zh: 随着团队开始围绕人工智能重新设计工作流程，他们逐渐积累了改进这些系统所需的经验。

sentences.en: We’re already seeing that in areas like software development, where AI-native teams are moving well beyond simple code generation toward entirely new ways of building software.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到，在软件开发等领域，人工智能原生团队正在远远超越简单的代码生成，转向全新的软件构建方式。

content_html_zh:
随着人工智能系统的不断发展和进步，受影响的不仅仅是数据中心架构，而是整个基础设施行业。

随着 Agentic AI 工作负载的不断扩展，CPU 层受到的影响尤其严重，效率、协调性和每项任务的成本成为越来越重要的决定因素。

我们采访了 Arm 云人工智能执行副总裁 Mohamed Awad，以了解更多信息。

  • Gartner 预测，到 2027 年，超过 40% 的代理人工智能项目将因运营困难而被取消。 Arm 的“系统级”架构方法如何具体解决导致这些取消的摩擦点，例如成本和复杂性？

我认为 Gartner 的预测强化了我们在整个行业中广泛听到的观点。 大多数组织之所以陷入困境，并不是因为当今的模型能力不够。 他们陷入困境是因为大规模实施人工智能与在试点中展示人工智能有着根本的不同。

在最大范围内，我们看到物理世界中也存在许多相同的运营挑战。 现在，构建人工智能基础设施意味着像计算的进步一样解决电力、供应链、土地、许可和部署时间表的问题。

从少量人工智能交互转向连续的生产级工作流程需要对基础设施堆栈有更全面的了解，但这也要求组织重新思考人工智能如何与其现有数据和业务流程交互。 人工智能在信息结构化且工作流程易于理解的情况下表现最佳。 随着组织将人工智能扩展到更复杂的企业环境中，基础设施和运营环境必须共同发展。

这就是为什么我们专注于优化系统，从 CPU 和平台到软件生态系统。 随着组织从试点转向生产，成功将越来越取决于整个基础设施协同工作的效率，而不仅仅是任何单个模型或处理器的能力。

订阅 TechRadar Pro 时事通讯，获取您的企业成功所需的所有热门新闻、观点、功能和指导！

  • 我们已经看到像 Uber 这样的公司由于非结构化的提示成本而在几个月内耗尽了他们的人工智能预算。 将智能从临时工具转移到以 Arm CPU 为基础的“中央智能层”会如何改变企业的经济投资回报率？

实际上，我对 Uber 这样的例子的看法略有不同。 它们并没有表明人工智能太昂贵，而是展示了成功部署人工智能后组织发现了多少价值。 挑战在于需求的增长速度快于经济上支持需求所需的基础设施的增长速度。

这就是为什么随着模型、芯片、软件和推理基础设施变得更加高效，我们看到人工智能代币经济以惊人的速度改善。 与此同时，组织正在学习重新设计工作流程，而不是简单地用人工智能替换现有流程。 这些趋势共同帮助人工智能的大规模部署变得更加经济。

Arm 的作用是通过从头开始优化人工智能基础设施来帮助提高效率。 提高整个计算平台的性能、内存带宽利用率和能源效率有助于在组织扩展人工智能时降低资本和运营成本。

  • 您认为人工智能真正的经济影响将来自于将人工智能转化为可靠的运营能力。 Arm 如何帮助企业从“随意实验”过渡到高吞吐量的日常业务运营？

当人工智能不再是人们偶尔使用的工具，而是成为企业运营结构的一部分时，就会发生最大的转变。 到那时，可靠性、延迟、安全性和效率就变得与模型能力一样重要。

我们的作用是提供计算基础，帮助实现大规模的转变。 我们是更广泛的行业努力的一部分，旨在跨芯片、平台和软件优化人工智能基础设施，以便组织可以在日常运营中更高效、更经济地部署人工智能。 最终，我们的目标不仅仅是实现工作自动化，而是让人工智能足够可靠，帮助人们在日常工作流程中完成更多工作。

  • 虽然 GPU 主导了人工智能的第一波浪潮，但“代理时代”似乎在协调层遇到了瓶颈。 为什么 CPU 现在是代理工作流程（可能检查 CRM、更新数据库并触发任务）是否真正成功的决定性因素？

GPU 仍然是训练模型和加速推理的基础。 正在改变的是围绕这些模型发生的一切。

每次代理检索企业数据、协调多个模型、调用外部工具或管理业务工作流程时，这些活动都严重依赖于 CPU。 随着组织部署更多自主人工智能系统，这些系统级工作负载不断增长，使得 CPU 成为提供高效人工智能基础设施的日益重要的组成部分。

问题不再是简单的“我能以多快的速度执行模型？” 问题是“我能多有效地执行整个人工智能工作流程？”

  • 与 x86 平台相比，新的 Arm AGI CPU 声称每个机架的性能提高了 2 倍以上。 在这个“历史性的首次”生产芯片中做出了哪些具体的架构选择来处理代理人工智能的连续、系统级工作负载？

代理人工智能对基础设施提出了与传统云计算根本不同的要求。 我们没有针对峰值基准性能进行优化，而是围绕现代 AI 数据中心的实际情况（固定功耗、冷却、机架密度和连续系统级工作负载）设计了 Arm AGI CPU。 这意味着优化数据在系统中的移动方式（从计算和内存带宽到高效的带宽利用），以便 CPU 可以协调代理 AI 创建的连续数据移动、协调和推理工作负载。

目标不仅仅是构建更快的 CPU。 它是为了帮助组织在日益定义人工智能基础设施的物理和经济限制内部署更有用的人工智能。

  • 随着 Oracle Cloud 加入 Arm AGI 生态系统以及 Google Cloud 部署 Axion，我们看到了向定制 Arm 芯片的巨大转变。 这是否标志着“通用”数据中心架构的终结，转而采用专门构建的代理基础设施？

我不认为这个故事是定制芯片与商业平台的对比。 正在发生的变化是，组织越来越希望基础设施能够针对其运行的人工智能工作负载进行优化，同时保持广泛软件生态系统的灵活性。

我们看到这种情况在 Arm 生态系统中以不同的方式发挥作用。 许多超大规模企业正在构建自己的芯片，同时还部署基于 Arm 的商用平台，包括 Arm AGI CPU。 这两种方法都反映了相同的基本趋势：人工智能基础设施变得更加专用，但客户仍然希望来自通用架构的可移植性和生态系统规模。

  • 许多代理人工智能项目都面临着超过数据中心容量的风险。 Arm 对每瓦性能的重视如何让组织能够在现有风冷数据中心内扩展代理 AI，而不需要大规模的新基础设施建设？

电力已成为人工智能基础设施的决定性经济约束之一。 组织不能假设他们总是有另一个数据中心或另一个可用的千兆瓦电力。

这改变了基础设施的设计方式。 成功越来越依赖于在现有电源、冷却和机架限制下提供更多人工智能功能。 每瓦性能不再只是一个工程指标，它正在成为一个业务指标，因为它决定了组织在不按比例增加基础设施投资的情况下可以部署多少人工智能。

  • 行业报告表明，人工智能将从根本上改变角色要求，奖励那些能够从“操作员”转变为“编排者”的人。 Arm 的硬件演变如何支持工作实际重新设计方式的转变？

随着人工智能嵌入到日常业务运营中，组织越来越需要支持持续协调而不是孤立的模型执行的基础设施。

无论是人们在编排人工智能代理，还是人工智能代理相互协调，底层基础设施都必须有效地管理持续的通信、上下文和执行。 这正是我们设计的系统级工作负载类型。 最终，我们的目标不是取代人类，而是让人工智能足够可靠，让人们可以花更少的时间协调工作，花更多的时间创造价值。

  • 当一批新的“人工智能原生”团队建立在代理就绪基础设施之上时，继续依赖传统行业范式的企业和专业人士面临哪些风险？

继续将人工智能视为独立生产力工具的组织可能会发现更难获得代理人工智能的全部运营优势。 下一阶段不仅仅是采用更多模型，而是构建能够支持整个企业持续人工智能运营的基础设施。

尽早开始构建这种能力的组织不仅会更快地部署人工智能，而且会学得更快。 随着团队开始围绕人工智能重新设计工作流程，他们逐渐积累了改进这些系统所需的经验。 我们已经看到，在软件开发等领域，人工智能原生团队正在远远超越简单的代码生成，转向全新的软件构建方式。
